name: Shami Kabab
description: Classic Pakistani shami kababs with tender beef and chana dal cooked until dry, ground with warm spices and herbs, then shaped and shallow-fried.
ingredients: 1 cup chana dal, rinsed and soaked for 30 minutes
½ cup fresh coriander and mint, chopped
method: Combine the beef, drained soaked chana dal, onion, ginger-garlic paste, cumin, coriander seeds, peppercorns, cloves, cinnamon and salt in a heavy pot. Add only enough water to cook the meat and dal tender.

Cover and simmer gently until both beef and dal are completely tender. Uncover near the end and cook while stirring until all visible excess moisture has evaporated; a wet mixture is difficult to shape.
Cool until safe to handle, remove the cinnamon or other large hard spice pieces if desired, then grind the mixture until cohesive and fairly smooth without adding water.
Mix in the green chillies, coriander and mint. Add the beaten egg a little at a time, stopping as soon as the mixture binds well enough to shape.
Form even flat patties and chill briefly if they feel soft. This also makes them easier to transfer to the pan without breaking.
Heat a thin layer of oil over medium heat and shallow-fry in batches, turning carefully after the first side has set, until both sides are golden and the kababs are thoroughly hot.
Drain briefly and serve with chutney, onion and lemon.
tips: The cooked beef-and-dal mixture must be quite dry before grinding.
Add egg gradually; too much liquid can make shami kababs fragile.
storage: Cool cooked kababs promptly and refrigerate covered. For longer storage, shaped uncooked kababs can be frozen separately until firm and then packed together.
image_alt: Pakistani shami kabab patties made with beef, chana dal, herbs and warm spices
image_caption: Shami kababs shaped from a dry, cohesive beef-and-chana-dal mixture and shallow-fried until golden.
technique: Moisture control happens before grinding. Beef and chana dal must be completely tender, then the cooking liquid must evaporate until the mixture is dry enough to grind into a cohesive paste. Egg is a final binder added only as needed.
doneness_cues: Chana dal should mash easily and beef should be tender before the pot is dried down.
No visible watery liquid should remain before grinding.
Ground mixture should hold a patty shape without leaking moisture.
Fried kababs should be golden outside and thoroughly hot through the centre.
mistakes: Adding the whole beaten egg automatically even when the mixture already binds.
Shaping while the mixture is hot and very soft.
Turning the patty before the first side has set.
substitutions: Use only as much beaten egg as the particular batch needs.
Green chilli and fresh herbs can be adjusted without changing the core beef-dal structure.
If a mixture is soft, chill it before adding dry filler.
reheating: Reheat gently in a lightly greased pan or oven until hot through; avoid prolonged frying that dries the patties.
serving: Serve with green chutney, sliced onion and lemon, or use in a bun kabab.

faqs.question: Why do shami kababs break?
faqs.answer: The mixture is often too wet, too warm or has too much egg. Dry the cooked mixture properly and chill before shaping if needed.

faqs.question: Why are my shami kababs dry?
faqs.answer: The beef-dal mixture may have been over-dried or the patties fried too long. Remove only excess water; the ground mixture should still feel cohesive.

faqs.question: Can shami kababs be frozen?
faqs.answer: Yes. Freeze shaped uncooked patties separately until firm, then pack them so they do not stick together.
